items.bold: PM MODI HYDERABAD SPEECH: "Use petrol, diesel, gas with GREAT RESTRAINT." OMC losses Rs 30,000 Cr/month. Hike before May 15.
items.text: The Week (3 hours ago), Oneindia (1 hour ago), and ANI confirmed: PM Narendra Modi, speaking at an inaugural event in Hyderabad on Sunday, said: "Today, the need of the hour is also to use petrol, gas, diesel and such things with great restraint. We have to use imported petro products only as per need. This will not only save foreign exchange but reduce the adverse impact of war." Modi also urged citizens to avoid purchasing gold for one year for weddings, revive work-from-home arrangements and online meetings, use Metro rail and public transport, adopt carpooling, and prefer railways for goods movement. Indian Oil, BPCL, and HPCL are together facing under-recoveries of approximately Rs 30,000 crore every month due to the gap between pump prices and international crude costs. Government and industry sources: petrol and diesel prices may be revised before May 15. If approved: hike of Rs 4-5/L. Ministry of Petroleum: LPG supply continues to be affected by the geopolitical situation — commercial LPG allocation increased to about 70 per cent of pre-crisis levels.

items.bold: PM MODI: Avoid gold for a year. Revive WFH. Use EVs and public transport. Farmers reduce fertiliser 50%.
items.text: News24/ANI and Hindustan Times confirmed the full scope of PM Modi's conservation appeal: (1) Gold: "I would appeal to people not to buy gold for weddings for one year" — gold imports are a major foreign exchange drain. (2) WFH: "During the Corona period, we adopted work from home, online meetings, video conferences. Today, the need of the hour is that we restart those practices." (3) Transport: Use Metro, public transport, carpooling, EVs wherever possible. Avoid unnecessary foreign travel, overseas vacations, foreign weddings. Choose domestic tourism. (4) Farmers: Reduce chemical fertiliser usage by 50%, move towards natural farming, adopt solar-powered irrigation pumps instead of diesel pumps. (5) Edible oil: Reduce consumption to benefit national economic health and personal health. This is the most comprehensive wartime conservation appeal by an Indian Prime Minister since the 1971 war. It signals the government has concluded that the crisis will be prolonged — and cannot be resolved by supply-side measures alone.

items.bold: OMC LOSSES Rs 30,000 Cr/MONTH. Petrol/diesel hike Rs 4-5/L BEFORE MAY 15 — most significant price signal of the war.
items.text: Oneindia (1 hour ago) confirmed: Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum together face under-recoveries of about Rs 30,000 crore every month due to the gap between local pump prices and international crude costs. India has so far avoided shortages and long queues at fuel pumps — but officials stressed this stability depends on careful planning. Government and industry officials: petrol and diesel prices may be revised before May 15. If approved: increase of around Rs 4 to Rs 5 per litre. This is the single most important domestic economic signal of the war: India has held pump prices steady for nearly four years — and is now on the verge of a war-driven hike. At Rs 5/L: petrol in Delhi would rise from Rs 94.77 to approximately Rs 99.77/L — approaching Rs 100/L for the first time ever. Every Rs 1/L hike adds approximately Rs 12,000 Cr annually to Indian household costs. A Rs 5/L hike = Rs 60,000 Cr annual consumer burden.

items.bold: BANGLADESH fuel rationing. SRI LANKA reduced working days. IEA largest-ever emergency stocks release. Global demand destruction.
items.text: Multiple outlets confirmed the regional and global picture: Bangladesh has imposed fuel rationing. Sri Lanka reduced official working days to manage the energy shortfall. IEA launched its largest ever release of emergency oil stocks and published a menu of demand-side measures — the IEA 2026 Energy Crisis Policy Response Tracker is now live, tracking government actions globally. India has so far avoided rationing, but Modi's conservation appeal signals the government is preparing citizens for potential tightening. The Oneindia report notes: "The same crisis has forced other countries to take tough steps." India's approach — voluntary conservation + imminent price hike rather than mandatory rationing — is calibrated to maintain social stability while reducing fiscal pressure on OMCs.

items.bold: INDIA SCENARIO CHANGE: Modi conservation speech + Rs 4-5/L hike before May 15 = war has reached Indian households formally.
items.text: Modi's Hyderabad speech changes the India scenario picture fundamentally: (1) The government has publicly acknowledged the crisis is structural and prolonged — not a temporary blip. (2) OMC hike before May 15 = petrol approaching Rs 100/L for first time ever. Consumer inflation impact: Rs 60,000 Cr annually from Rs 5/L hike. (3) WFH revival + public transport appeal = economic activity slowdown is now government-endorsed. GDP impact: voluntary WFH reduces urban fuel consumption but also reduces productivity. (4) Gold purchase moratorium: gold imports run Rs 3-4 lakh Cr annually — if households comply, significant forex saving. (5) Fertiliser 50% reduction: farmers are being asked to absorb the kharif input shock. (6) Farmers to switch to solar pumps: long-term good, short-term transition cost. (7) LPG at 70% of pre-crisis commercial allocation: food service, hospitality, and industrial sectors operating at constrained capacity. Modi has formally moved India from "managing the war's impact" to "adapting to the war as a new normal."

military.t: CNN SATELLITE: US Fighter Jet Attacked Iranian Ship Saturday. Iran Warns "HEAVY ASSAULT" if Attacks Continue.
military.d: CNN live (4 minutes ago) confirmed: Satellite imagery shows smoke billowing from an Iranian-flagged ship on Saturday after a US fighter jet attack. CNN's live blog headline: "Iran warns US of heavy assault if ships face more attacks during ceasefire." This is a new confirmed kinetic incident — a US F/A-18 or equivalent fighter jet attacked an Iranian-flagged vessel on Saturday. The satellite smoke signature provides visual confirmation. Iran's response: the Army's spokesperson Brigadier General Akraminia warned Sunday that Iran will conduct a "heavy assault" if ships face more attacks during the ceasefire. Both sides are now attacking each other's vessels while calling it a ceasefire. US: it is defensive (Project Freedom framework). Iran: it is a ceasefire violation. The gap in legal frameworks is as wide as the kinetic gap is narrow.

military.t: IRAN GENERAL AKRAMINIA: "Countries Enforcing US Sanctions Will Face Problems at Hormuz." Threat Broadened.
military.d: CNN live (Sunday) confirmed: Brigadier General Amir Akraminia, Iranian Army spokesperson: "From now on, countries that follow the United States in enforcing sanctions against the Islamic Republic of Iran will certainly face problems passing through the Strait of Hormuz." This is Iran's most significant broadening of Hormuz threats beyond the bilateral US-Iran framework. It targets any nation enforcing US sanctions: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, EU member states, South Korea, Japan. Kuwait alone reported over 1,000 missiles and drones fired toward its territory before the April 8 ceasefire. The Akraminia warning means Iran is now threatening the entire sanctions-enforcing international community with Hormuz disruption — a fundamental escalation in the scope of the Hormuz threat. For the 40-nation multinational initiative (Charles de Gaulle): this threat signals Iran is prepared to confront a coalition, not just the US Navy.

military.t: IRAN HAS RESPONDED to US Proposal — FM Confirmed Sunday. Transmitted via Pakistan Mediators.
military.d: CNN live and CBS News confirmed Sunday morning: Iran has sent its formal response to the US proposal via Pakistan mediators. Iranian FM confirmed the response was transmitted. Content not yet publicly confirmed as of 10:15 AM IST. This is the most consequential diplomatic document of the 72-day war. If Iran accepts the nuclear moratorium framework (enrichment moratorium, US lifts sanctions, frozen funds released, Hormuz reopens): deal possible within 24-48 hours. Brent would fall to $85-90, Sensex would surge 1,500-2,000 points Monday. If Iran adds new conditions or rejects key nuclear points: Murkowski AUMF introduction Monday becomes near-certain. The Iran response timing — Sunday morning, day before Murkowski AUMF — may be deliberate: give the WH ammunition to delay the AUMF while Iran continues to negotiate.

military.t: WHITE HOUSE HASSETT: "Gusher of Oil" When Hormuz Opens. CHARLES DE GAULLE Heading to Red Sea.
military.d: Fox News Sunday Morning Futures confirmed: White House Kevin Hassett: once Hormuz fully opened, "a gusher of oil will be released into the market and bring prices down." This is the White House's market expectation for a deal. Brent at $80 (Emkay call) from current $101 = $21/barrel fall = India annual import bill saving of Rs 120,000+ Cr. Separately: France's Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier heading to southern Red Sea. Macron: "France ready to secure Hormuz and capable of doing so." 40-nation multinational initiative confirmed. A French carrier group in the Red Sea approach + 40 nations = the multilateral force Iran now faces. Akraminia's "heavy assault" warning is partly directed at this coalition. Iran is signalling the cost of forced reopening to deter the Charles de Gaulle approach.

military.t: MURKOWSKI AUMF May 11 — Senate Returns TOMORROW. Iran Response = WH Claims Progress = AUMF May Delay.
military.d: Multiple outlets confirmed: Murkowski AUMF measure due May 11 when Senate returns from recess. However: Iran has now sent a formal response to the US proposal. The White House can tell Murkowski: "We have Iran's response — give us 48 to 72 hours to review it." If Murkowski accepts: AUMF delayed, markets calm. If Murkowski proceeds regardless: Senate debate on formally authorizing or ending the war begins. The Iran response Sunday morning may have been timed deliberately to give the WH this ammunition. Strategic simultaneity: Iran avoids AUMF pressure on the WH while also avoiding formal rejection of the deal. Murkowski's decision Monday — proceed with AUMF or hold — will be the first major congressional signal of the week.

assessment.headline: DAY 72, 6PM SUN: PM MODI: "Use petrol, gas, diesel with GREAT RESTRAINT." OMC LOSSES Rs 30,000 Cr/MONTH. HIKE Rs 4-5/L BEFORE MAY 15. GOLD MORATORIUM. WFH REVIVAL. MODI HAS FORMALLY MOVED INDIA FROM CRISIS MANAGEMENT TO CRISIS ADAPTATION. THE WAR IS NOW INDIA'S NEW NORMAL.
assessment.body:
Sunday 6:00 PM IST. Day 72. PM Modi has fundamentally changed India's domestic scenario.

PM MODI'S HYDERABAD SPEECH — THE FULL PICTURE
"Today, the need of the hour is also to use petrol, gas, diesel and such things with great restraint. We have to use imported petro products only as per need. This will not only save foreign exchange but reduce the adverse impact of war."

THE SIX CONSERVATION APPEALS
1. Petrol/diesel/LPG: use only as per need, with great restraint
2. Gold: do not buy for weddings for one year
3. WFH: revive COVID-era work-from-home, online meetings, video conferencing
4. Transport: Metro, public transport, carpooling, EVs. Avoid unnecessary foreign travel.
5. Farmers: reduce chemical fertiliser by 50%, move to natural farming, solar pumps
6. Edible oil: reduce consumption

WHY THIS SPEECH CHANGES THE SCENARIO
This is not a routine public address. It is the Indian PM formally signalling to 1.4 billion citizens that:
• The energy crisis is structural and prolonged — not temporary
• The government cannot fully absorb the war's cost
• Citizens must change behaviour — voluntarily, but from the highest authority
• The war in West Asia is now a matter of Indian household economics
No Indian PM has made this scale of conservation appeal since the 1971 war.

THE OMC HIKE — THE MOST CERTAIN DOMESTIC DEVELOPMENT OF THE WEEK
• Indian Oil + BPCL + HPCL: Rs 30,000 Cr/month in under-recoveries
• Hike of Rs 4-5/L on petrol and diesel expected before May 15
• Petrol in Delhi: approaching Rs 100/L for first time ever
• Every Rs 1/L = Rs 12,000 Cr annual consumer burden
• Rs 5/L hike = Rs 60,000 Cr annual consumer burden
• Inflation impact: 35bps CPI per $10/bbl crude rise — now compounded by price hike

THE REGIONAL CONTEXT
• Bangladesh: fuel rationing imposed
• Sri Lanka: working days reduced
• IEA: largest-ever emergency oil stocks release
• India: voluntary conservation + imminent hike (no rationing yet)
India is managing better than its neighbours — but is now formally in crisis mode.

THE INTERNATIONAL PICTURE UNCHANGED
• Iran has formally responded to US proposal (content pending)
• US fighter jet attacked Iranian ship Saturday (CNN satellite confirmed)
• Iran threatens "heavy assault" + warns sanction-enforcing nations on Hormuz
• Charles de Gaulle heading to Red Sea
• Murkowski AUMF May 11
• Hassett: "gusher of oil" when Hormuz opens

VERDICT: Day 72 evening marks a turning point in India's domestic relationship with the West Asia War. From today, India is not watching a war from a distance — it is managing its domestic economy around the war's permanent presence. Modi's conservation speech, the imminent Rs 5/L hike, and the LPG supply constraints confirm that the government has concluded this war will not end quickly and India must adapt. The Hassett "gusher of oil" and the Iran response offer hope of resolution. But Modi's speech to 1.4 billion Indians on a Sunday afternoon says something different: plan for the war to continue. India now has two simultaneous truths: a diplomatic track hoping for a deal, and a domestic track adapting to the war as a new economic reality.
